evidence.title: Manmohan Singh govt's lasting legacy: RTI Act
evidence.key_figure: RTI Bill introduced December 2004; passed Lok Sabha 11 May 2005 and Rajya Sabha 12 May 2005; implemented 12 October 2005

claim.analysis:
The Indian National Congress's 2004 Lok Sabha manifesto carried a right-to-information commitment, and the UPA's National Common Minimum Programme also promised an RTI Act.

The Right to Information Bill was introduced in Parliament in December 2004, passed by the Lok Sabha on 11 May 2005 and by the Rajya Sabha on 12 May 2005, and received the President's assent on 15 June 2005; the Act came fully into force on 12 October 2005.

The Indian Express, reviewing the Manmohan Singh government's record, describes the Act as the fulfilment of the 2004 manifesto promise, while noting that the CBI was exempted from its purview in 2010 during the same government's term.
claim.notes: Manifesto release date approximate (2004); the exact sentence on RTI in the 2004 manifesto could not be retrieved, so quote_is_verbatim is false and the wording is paraphrased. The link between the 2004 manifesto and the RTI Act is documented by The Indian Express. The rti.gov.in URL was identified via the Wikipedia RTI page and was not separately fetched.
